intro: A quick check on splitting a force into parts.

widget.instructions: Tick Tilted axes to measure forces along and across the slope. The weight is fixed; you can explore its components before answering.

stem: A block on a slope inclined at {{theta}}° has a weight of {{W}} N.
What is the component of its weight along the slope (down the slope)?

hints.text: Turn on the tilted axes: one runs along the slope, the other straight out of it.
The angle between the weight and the line perpendicular to the slope equals the slope angle θ. Which side of that triangle lies along the slope?
The part along the slope is opposite θ in the triangle, so it is W sin θ.

sin-cos-swap-incline.text: That is the part pressing into the slope, W cos θ. The angle θ sits between the weight and the slope's perpendicular, so the part along the slope is the side opposite θ: W sin θ.

whole-weight-along-slope.text: Only part of the weight acts along the slope; the rest presses into it. Split the weight along the tilted axes.

dimension-mismatch.text: A component of a force is itself a force, in newtons.

generic.text: Split the weight along the slope and perpendicular to it, then pick the part that lies along the slope.

workedSolution.text: Use axes along and perpendicular to the slope.
The angle between the weight and the perpendicular to the slope is θ = {{theta}}°, so along the slope: W sin θ = {{W}} × sin {{theta}}° = {{along}} N.
Into the slope: W cos θ = {{perp}} N. Together the two parts rebuild the {{W}} N weight.

sin-cos-swap-incline.front: Which component of weight acts along a slope of angle θ?
sin-cos-swap-incline.back: W sin θ along the slope; W cos θ into it.

whole-weight-along-slope.front: Does all of a block's weight pull it down a slope?
whole-weight-along-slope.back: No. Only W sin θ acts along the slope; W cos θ presses into it.

generic.front: Weight component along a θ slope?
